correctness.rationale: For six distinct unit normals sum x_i=0 and sum x_i x_i^T=2I, E=M^TM/2 is a rank-three projector orthogonal to the all-ones vector, and its complement F=I-J/6-E is a rank-two constant-diagonal 1/3 projector. Six unit-modulus complex coordinates z_i obey sum z_i=sum z_i^2=0; self-inversive symmetry forces characteristic polynomial z^6-e3 z^3+e6 and partitions them into two equilateral triples. The original normals therefore split into two orthonormal triples with opposite sums; one twist phi in [0,pi/3] parametrizes all configurations. The polar unit-support hexahedron/prism has area A0=18t/(t+1)^2 per normal and volume 36t/(t+1)^2, t=2cos(pi/3-phi); scale to facet areas 2pi/3 to obtain V=4pi^(3/2)(t+1)/(9sqrt(3t)), increasing across t in [1,2]. Exact endpoint volumes 8pi^(3/2)/(9sqrt3) and (2pi/3)^(3/2) with triangular bipyramid/cube shapes. Degenerate endpoint treated; numerical convex hulls are supplementary, not universal proof.
